input.quote: Contractor shall cause its personnel at Company's facility to comply with Company's (i) safety and security rules and other rules applicable to those working in the facility, and (ii) Company's policies concerning access to and security of any Company computer system to which Contractor may have access
input.rationale: No redline is proposed because the AUDIT rule is protective of us and there is nothing in the Agreement to constrain. Full-text searches for "audit", "inspect" and "verif" return no hits, and "records" appears only in the IP-ownership (§4(b)) and confidentiality (§7) provisions. RadialSpark has no right to audit, inspect or verify Clear Capital's records, usage or systems: §3 runs one way in our favour (Contractor must give us invoice-level supporting detail and expense receipts); §4(c) grants us a royalty-free perpetual license with no reporting, self-certification or audit trigger; and the only system-access language, §1(c) quoted above, restricts Contractor's access to our systems under our own security policies rather than granting any verification right. The deterministic "audit frequency limited" check fails only because there is no audit clause to match — an artefact of absence, not evidence of a deviation, since no frequency, notice, cost-allocation or system-access term binds us. That position is better than the preferred one (annual, 30 days' notice, independent auditor, Vendor cost unless underpayment exceeds 5%, no direct system access), so flagging it would risk inviting an audit right we do not currently concede. Noted for the file: if a Statement of Work later introduces a records-inspection or verification right, we should apply those preferred limits, falling back to annual audits on 15 days' notice at Contractor's cost unless underpayment exceeds 10%.
